reference.source: Textbook of Pediatric Rheumatology / ILAR & PRINTO criteria
clinicalPearls: A post-infectious hyperinflammatory syndrome occurring weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, with features overlapping Kawasaki disease and toxic shock
Presents with persistent high fever plus multisystem involvement, commonly gastrointestinal (abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhoea that can mimic an acute abdomen), mucocutaneous, and cardiovascular
Cardiac involvement is prominent, including myocardial dysfunction, shock, coronary artery dilatation or aneurysm and conduction abnormalities
Markedly raised inflammatory markers, along with elevated ferritin, D-dimer, natriuretic peptides and cardiac troponin, are typical
Evidence of recent or current SARS-CoV-2 infection (positive serology, PCR or a clear exposure) supports the diagnosis
Distinguishing MIS-C from severe acute COVID-19, Kawasaki disease and bacterial sepsis is essential and time-critical
Treatment centres on immunomodulation with IVIG and corticosteroids, with biologic therapy for refractory cases and supportive intensive care for shock
reference.pathophysiology: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children is a delayed, dysregulated immune response following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Weeks after exposure, an exaggerated adaptive and innate immune reaction, with widespread cytokine release, endothelial activation and, in some, superantigen-like T-cell stimulation, produces a hyperinflammatory, vasculitic state. This drives multiorgan injury, most notably myocardial dysfunction, vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock, and coronary artery involvement reminiscent of Kawasaki disease, together with a systemic inflammatory and prothrombotic milieu.
additionalDifferentials: Bacterial sepsis and toxic shock syndrome
Appendicitis or other surgical acute abdomen
Macrophage activation syndrome or systemic JIA flare
additionalInvestigations: Inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein), ferritin and full blood count
Cardiac troponin and natriuretic peptides with electrocardiography and echocardiography for cardiac assessment and coronary imaging
SARS-CoV-2 PCR and serology plus documentation of exposure
Coagulation studies including D-dimer and fibrinogen
Blood cultures and infection screen to exclude sepsis
Renal and liver function and electrolytes
Imaging of the abdomen when a surgical cause is being considered
redFlags: Signs of shock, hypotension or poor perfusion requiring urgent resuscitation
Myocardial dysfunction, arrhythmia or coronary artery aneurysm on echocardiography
Rapid clinical deterioration despite initial treatment
Features suggesting macrophage activation or disseminated intravascular coagulation
Altered consciousness or other severe organ dysfunction
reference.prognosis: With prompt immunomodulation and intensive supportive care, most children recover, including recovery of myocardial function, though a minority sustain persistent cardiac abnormalities such as coronary aneurysms. Early recognition and treatment are the main determinants of outcome, and structured cardiology follow-up is recommended.
pitfalls: Mistaking the prominent gastrointestinal presentation for a purely surgical abdomen
Anchoring on acute COVID-19 and missing the delayed hyperinflammatory picture
Underestimating cardiac involvement by not obtaining early echocardiography and cardiac biomarkers
Delaying immunomodulatory treatment in a deteriorating child
Failing to arrange cardiac follow-up after recovery
references: WHO and RCPCH case definitions for MIS-C/PIMS-TS
management: First-line immunomodulation with intravenous immunoglobulin, usually combined with corticosteroids, to dampen the hyperinflammatory response
Escalation to biologic therapy with interleukin-1 or interleukin-6 antagonists such as anakinra or tocilizumab for refractory or severe disease
Haemodynamic support for vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock, with fluid resuscitation, vasoactive and inotropic agents and intensive-care monitoring
Antithrombotic therapy with antiplatelet aspirin and anticoagulation guided by coronary involvement and thrombotic risk
Empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics until bacterial sepsis and toxic shock syndrome are excluded
Cardiac surveillance with serial echocardiography, electrocardiography and cardiac biomarkers for myocardial dysfunction, arrhythmia and coronary artery aneurysms
Manage within a paediatric multidisciplinary team spanning rheumatology, cardiology, infectious diseases and intensive care, with structured cardiology follow-up after discharge
